title: Audit Export SLOs & Error Budgets (SIEM-ready audit export beta)
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
## Overview
This page defines the Service Level Objectives (SLOs), Service Level Indicators (SLIs), and alerting thresholds for **SIEM-ready audit export (beta)**.

Audit export allows customers to deliver Redwood audit events to customer-managed destinations (initial sinks: **Splunk HEC**, **Datadog Logs intake**, **S3**). The system provides **at-least-once delivery**, durable buffering, retries/backoff, and explicit failure states per destination. Duplicates are possible by design; the schema provides stable dedupe keys.

This SLO spec is used by SRE for:
- Launch readiness (beta enablement / staged rollout)
- On-call paging policy
- Dashboards and weekly review
- Error budget policy and reliability work prioritization

---

## Scope
### In-scope
- Delivery worker subsystem: queueing, retries/backoff, DLQ, checkpointing
- Sink connectors: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, S3 writer
- Per-destination health/state reporting (enabled/paused/degraded)
- End-to-end event delivery latency as observed by exporter instrumentation

### Out-of-scope / not covered by SLO
- SIEM vendor-side indexing latency after acceptance (e.g., Splunk searchability delay)
- Customer-managed network outages beyond our control (tracked separately as *customer-caused errors*)
- Historical backfill for all tenants (beta non-goal)

---

## Definitions
### What counts as an “event”
An event is a single Audit Event v1 record emitted by Redwood’s audit logging pipeline and presented to the audit-export worker for a destination after filtering.

### “Delivered” (per sink)
We count an event as **delivered** when the sink confirms acceptance:
- **Splunk HEC:** HTTP 200 from /services/collector/event. If HEC ACK mode is enabled, delivery time is recorded at ACK confirmation (HEC /ack endpoint). If ACK mode is disabled, delivery is recorded at 200 response.
- **Datadog Logs intake:** HTTP 200/202 from intake endpoint. (We do not wait for downstream parsing pipelines.)
- **S3:** Successful PutObject (or multipart completion) and object metadata write success.

### End-to-end delivery latency
**Delivery latency** is measured as:
- `delivered_at - emitted_at`

Where:
- `emitted_at` is from the audit event payload
- `delivered_at` is set by the delivery worker at the time the sink acceptance condition is met

We also track internal sub-latencies for diagnosis:
- queue wait time
- connector request time
- retry time accumulated

### “Success rate” (delivery)
For the purpose of SLOs, success rate is computed as:
- `delivered_events / eligible_events`

Where `eligible_events` are events that:
- pass destination filter rules
- are associated with an enabled destination
- are not explicitly dropped by validation (schema/size hard-fail)

Events dropped due to invalid destination configuration (e.g., invalid URL) are attributed as **configuration errors** and counted as failures.

### Customer-caused vs Redwood-caused failures
We classify connector failures into:
- **Customer-caused (tracked, not excluded from paging by default):** auth failures (401/403), DNS resolution to customer host failing, customer TLS misconfiguration, 4xx due to token disabled, explicit customer firewall blocks.
- **Redwood-caused:** 5xx from our infrastructure, queue corruption, worker crash loops, regression in connector logic, internal throttling mis-tuned.

We do not exclude customer-caused errors from the SLI; customers experience them as “export not working.” We *do* use classification to route response (Support vs Eng vs customer guidance) and to avoid false positives across many tenants.

---

## SLOs (Hosted vs Private)
We maintain separate targets due to different operational control and network variability.

### Window, aggregation, and weighting
- **Evaluation window:** rolling **28 days**
- **Aggregation:** per destination, then rolled up across destinations by event count
- **Dimensions:** `deployment_mode` (hosted|private), `destination_type` (splunk|datadog|s3), `region`

### SLO table
| SLO | Hosted target | Private target | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| End-to-end delivery latency (P99) | **≤ 5 minutes** | **≤ 10 minutes** | Computed over delivered events. Used to detect backlog/slowdown. |
| End-to-end delivery latency (P50) | **≤ 60 seconds** | **≤ 120 seconds** | Early signal for queueing and connector slowness. |
| Delivery success rate | **≥ 99.95%** | **≥ 99.5%** | Success = accepted by sink (or ACK if enabled for Splunk). |
| Backlog bound (oldest event age) | **≤ 15 minutes** (99% of time) | **≤ 30 minutes** (99% of time) | Guardrail SLO; evaluated as time-in-bounds. |
| DLQ growth (operational guardrail) | **0 sustained growth** (weekly) | **0 sustained growth** (weekly) | Not a formal SLO; triggers operational action and postmortem if breached. |

#### Rationale (beta)
- The beta UX and customer promises are centered on “near-real-time” security monitoring. Most design partners consider >15 minutes to be operationally painful.
- Private deployments have more dependency on customer egress policy, DNS, and customer-owned endpoints.
- Success rate targets are intentionally asymmetric (Hosted higher) to reflect operational control.

---

## SLIs (how we measure)
### Primary SLIs
1) **Delivery latency SLI**
- Metric: `audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds` (histogram)
- Tags: `deployment_mode`, `destination_id`, `destination_type`, `region`
- Computation:
  - P50 / P99 from histogram for each deployment_mode

2) **Delivery success rate SLI**
- Metric numerator: `audit_export_delivered_total`
- Metric denominator: `audit_export_eligible_total`
- Additional metrics for diagnosis:
  - `audit_export_send_attempts_total`
  - `audit_export_send_failures_total` tagged by `error_class` (auth|throttle|5xx|timeout|schema|config)

3) **Backlog bound SLI**
- Metric: `audit_export_queue_oldest_event_age_seconds` (gauge)
- We evaluate “in bounds” as:
  - Hosted: <= 900s
  - Private: <= 1800s
- Metric: `audit_export_queue_depth` (gauge) is tracked but not used directly in SLO math (depth can be misleading without rate context)

### Data quality requirements
- All workers must emit telemetry even when destinations are paused/degraded.
- We must record `delivered_at` consistently across connectors.
- For Splunk with ACK enabled, we must emit separate metrics:
  - `audit_export_splunk_ack_wait_seconds`

---

## Error budget policy
### Error budget math
- **Success rate SLO** error budget (Hosted): 0.05% failed eligible events per 28 days
- **Success rate SLO** error budget (Private): 0.5% failed eligible events per 28 days

Latency and backlog SLOs are evaluated independently; persistent latency/backlog breaches usually precede success-rate degradation.

### Policy actions
If we breach or are projected to breach an SLO:
1) **Immediate:** freeze risky changes to audit-export workers/connectors unless they mitigate the issue
2) **Within 2 business days:** create an ENG reliability follow-up (bugfix, scaling, retry tuning, circuit breaker improvements)
3) **Within 5 business days:** SRE + owning team review: adjust alerts, update runbook, confirm dashboards cover root cause signals
4) **For repeated breaches:** require launch review for new destinations/features (e.g., additional sinks) and/or raise minimum platform prerequisites for Private

---

## Alerting thresholds
We use multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerting for the success-rate SLO and direct threshold alerts for backlog/latency.

### Paging principles
- Page only for issues that require operator action to prevent or mitigate customer impact.
- Prefer per-destination pages only when blast radius is constrained; otherwise page globally.
- Use error classification to route: auth/config issues should typically create Support-facing playbooks and customer guidance, not noisy paging.

### Alerts (Hosted)
1) **SLO burn rate (success rate) – page**
- Condition (multi-window):
  - 2h burn rate > 14x AND 24h burn rate > 4x
- Signal: ratio of `audit_export_send_failures_total` / `audit_export_eligible_total`
- Page: `#oncall-sre` + `audit-export` responder

2) **Backlog oldest age – page**
- `audit_export_queue_oldest_event_age_seconds > 900` for 15 minutes
- Additional gating: `audit_export_eligible_total` rate > minimal baseline (avoid paging on idle systems)

3) **Delivery latency P99 – ticket**
- P99 `audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds` > 300 for 30 minutes
- Creates Jira ticket to SRE + Platform Control Plane owner

4) **DLQ growth – page (high severity)**
- `audit_export_dlq_events_total` increasing AND `audit_export_dlq_events_total > 1000` within 1 hour (per region)
- Rationale: DLQ implies durable non-delivery requiring replay/triage

### Alerts (Private)
Private environments vary; we use softer thresholds and emphasize backlog and connector health.

1) **Backlog oldest age – page**
- `audit_export_queue_oldest_event_age_seconds > 1800` for 20 minutes

2) **Success rate burn – ticket by default, page if widespread**
- Ticket if:
  - 6h burn rate > 6x AND 3d burn rate > 2x
- Page if:
  - More than 3 private installations (distinct `cluster_id`) are breaching simultaneously (indicates shared regression)

3) **Connector error spikes – ticket**
- `audit_export_send_failures_total{error_class="auth"}` sustained > threshold (per cluster) => route to Solutions Engineering / customer
- `audit_export_send_failures_total{error_class="5xx"}` sustained => route to Engineering

### Alert routing and ownership
- Primary: SRE on-call (Hosted) or Private on-call rotation (Private)
- Secondary: Platform Control Plane (control-plane APIs/state), Security Eng (schema/PII/export policy), Console (customer-visible health)

---

## Operational dashboards
Dashboards must include (minimum):
- Success rate by destination_type and region (stacked by error_class)
- Delivery latency P50/P90/P99 by destination_type
- Queue depth and oldest event age
- Retry rate and attempt distribution
- DLQ volume and top DLQ reasons
- Destination state counts (enabled/paused/degraded)

Canonical dashboard:
- "Audit Export – SLO Overview" (Observability Pack)

---

## Runbooks
Primary runbook:
- **Audit export: backlog drain & replay** (see related pages)

Runbook must cover:
- Diagnosing lag vs sink outage vs credential failures
- Pausing a destination safely to stop retry storms
- Backoff tuning and circuit breaker behavior
- Draining backlog without overwhelming sinks
- DLQ triage and replaying a bounded time window (with safeguards)

---

## Change log
- 2025-01-22: Initial SLO targets for beta (Hosted/Private split), added backlog guardrail and DLQ alerting.
- 2025-02-10: Updated Splunk delivery definition to reflect optional HEC ACK mode; tightened Hosted backlog paging to 15 min sustained; clarified customer-caused failure handling.
